How to use this book

IMPULSE LEARNING CENTER
1. Read the model

Read the model text. Find the highlighted phrases and notice how the text is organised.

2. Learn the language

Study the Language focus and the Words & phrases, then do the practice.

3. Plan

Make short notes for each paragraph before you start writing.

4. Write and check

Write your text, then use the Self-check list. Compare with the model answers.

Each unit has seven parts

1 · Model text

A real example of the unit’s text type.

2 · Language focus

One writing skill with examples.

3 · Words & phrases

Ten useful collocations with Uzbek.

4 · Practice

Use the new words in sentences.

5 · Plan

Notes for each paragraph.

6 · Writing task

A real-life task with lines to write on.

7 · IELTS-style task

An IELTS Task 2-style essay with ideas and a four-paragraph plan.

A good essay

IntroductionNowadays, many people move to big cities. This trend has both advantages and disadvantages.
Body 1The main advantage is that cities offer more jobs. For example, …
Body 2However, cities can become crowded and expensive. Moreover, …
ConclusionIn conclusion, moving to a city can improve people’s lives, but …

UNIT1

Free Time

Text type: Informal letter · Opinion essay

4pages
UNIT 1.1 · MODEL TEXT · INFORMAL LETTER

Re: How are things?

Dear Sam,

Thanks a lot for your letter – it was lovely to hear from you and to see the photos from your camping trip!

You asked me about my free time. Well, life has been pretty busy since I started my new course, so I don’t have as much free time as before. During the week I usually go to the gym after class, and I’ve recently taken up chess – I play online with a friend most evenings.

At the weekend I try to have a lie-in on Saturday and then I hang out with my friends in the city centre. We often go for a walk or have a coffee.

Anyway, I’d better go now – I’ve got a huge to-do list! Why don’t you come and visit in the summer? We could go camping together.

Hope to hear from you soon.

All the best,

Bekzod

Find the highlighted phrases. Which ones can you use in your own writing?

UNIT 1.2 · LANGUAGE FOCUS

Features of an informal letter

Informal letters (IELTS General Training Task 1) are written to friends. Use contractions, phrasal verbs and friendly phrases, and organise your ideas in short paragraphs – one for each point in the task.

  • OpenThanks a lot for your letter. / It was lovely to hear from you.
  • ReplyYou asked me about … / As for …
  • Change topicAnyway, … / By the way, …
  • SuggestWhy don’t you … ? / How about … -ing?
  • CloseHope to hear from you soon. / All the best, / Take care,

  • phones and the internet fill every free minute
  • machines and online services save us time

  3. 3
    Body paragraph 2

    On the other hand, … / However, … Moreover, …

  4. 4
    Conclusion

    In conclusion, … / To sum up, I believe …

UNIT2

City Life

Text type: Article for a website · Advantages & disadvantages essay

4pages
UNIT 2.1 · MODEL TEXT · ARTICLE FOR A WEBSITE

My city: Tashkent

If you are looking for a city with a great mix of old and new, Tashkent is the place for you.

The city centre is lively and modern, with wide streets, parks and tower blocks. The metro, which is one of the most beautiful in the world, is cheap and reliable. In the old town, where you can visit Chorsu Bazaar, life is very different: narrow streets, busy stalls and friendly street sellers.

Of course, it isn’t perfect. The traffic can be terrible in the rush hour, and some areas are crowded in summer.

All in all, though, Tashkent is a safe and welcoming city. I would definitely recommend spending a few days here – you won’t regret it!

Find the highlighted phrases. Which ones can you use in your own writing?

UNIT 2.2 · LANGUAGE FOCUS

Relative clauses and describing places

Use relative clauses to add information without starting a new sentence. In an article, start with a question or a strong sentence to interest the reader, and finish with a recommendation.

  • whichThe metro, which is very cheap, is the best way to travel.
  • whereThe old town, where my grandparents live, is very quiet.
  • whoThe street sellers, who are very friendly, sell everything.
  • HookIf you are looking for … , … is the place for you.
  • EndingAll in all, … / I would definitely recommend …

UNIT3

Feelings and Actions

Text type: Story · Discussion essay

4pages
UNIT 3.1 · MODEL TEXT · STORY

Stuck!

It was a hot afternoon in July and I was on my way to a job interview. I had left home early because I wanted to be on time.

While I was waiting for the lift on the ninth floor, I felt nervous but excited. I stepped inside and pressed the button. Suddenly, the lift stopped between two floors and the lights went out.

At first I panicked and pushed every button. Then I took a deep breath and calmly called the number on the wall. A voice on the intercom told me that a rescue team was coming.

Forty minutes later, the doors opened. I was exhausted and embarrassed, but the manager just smiled and said, “You must be our candidate!”

To my surprise, I got the job. I’ll never forget that day.

Find the highlighted phrases. Which ones can you use in your own writing?

UNIT 3.2 · LANGUAGE FOCUS

Narrative tenses and adverbs

Use the past simple for the main events, the past continuous for background actions, and the past perfect for things that happened earlier. Adverbs and feelings make the story come alive.

  • Past simpleThe lift stopped. I pressed the button.
  • Past continuousWhile I was waiting, I felt nervous.
  • Past perfectI had left home early, so I wasn’t late.
  • Adverbssuddenly · calmly · nervously · luckily · eventually
  • Feelingsanxious · embarrassed · exhausted · relieved · frightened

UNIT4

Life Events

Text type: Blog post: a turning point · Opinion essay

4pages
UNIT 4.1 · MODEL TEXT · BLOG POST: A TURNING POINT

The year that changed my life

I’ll never forget the day I left home. I was eighteen and I had just passed my university entrance exam.

At first, life in the capital was hard. I shared a small flat with two other students, and for the first few weeks I missed my family terribly. I had never cooked for myself or paid bills before.

However, as soon as I made some friends, things got easier. I learned to manage my money, I took up running, and eventually I found a part-time job in a café.

Since then, I’ve become much more independent and confident. Looking back, leaving home was the best decision I’ve ever made, because it taught me to take responsibility for my own life.

Find the highlighted phrases. Which ones can you use in your own writing?

UNIT 4.2 · LANGUAGE FOCUS

Time linkers for life stories

Use time linkers to show when things happened and how a situation developed. Use the present perfect (since then, I’ve become …) to connect the past with now.

  • BeginningAt first, … / When I was … / In my late teens, …
  • Sequenceas soon as · after · before · then · later
  • Durationfor the first few weeks · during that year · until
  • Resulteventually · in the end · finally
  • NowSince then, I’ve … / Looking back, …

UNIT5

Money and Possessions

Text type: Formal letter of complaint · Advantages & disadvantages essay

4pages
UNIT 5.1 · MODEL TEXT · FORMAL LETTER OF COMPLAINT

Faulty headphones

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a pair of wireless headphones which I bought from your online shop on 12 March (order number 58214).

When the parcel arrived, the headphones looked brand new. However, after only two days the left side stopped working, and the battery now lasts less than an hour. I was extremely disappointed, as the headphones cost £120 and were advertised as “high quality”.

I have tried to contact your customer service team twice by phone, but nobody has called me back.

I would be grateful if you could send me a full refund or a replacement pair as soon as possible. I have attached a copy of the receipt.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,

Laylo Karimova

Find the highlighted phrases. Which ones can you use in your own writing?

UNIT 5.2 · LANGUAGE FOCUS

Writing a formal complaint

In IELTS General Training Task 1 you may need to complain. Explain the facts clearly, say how you feel politely, and say exactly what you want the company to do. Do not use contractions or slang.

  • PurposeI am writing to complain about …
  • FactsI bought … on … / When it arrived, …
  • ProblemHowever, … / Unfortunately, …
  • FeelingI was extremely disappointed / surprised that …
  • ActionI would be grateful if you could … / I would like a full refund.

UNIT 6.1 · MODEL TEXT · SEMI-FORMAL LETTER TO A NEIGHBOUR

A problem with noise

Dear Mr Collins,

My name is Nodira and I live in flat 12, just below yours. I hope you don’t mind me writing to you about something that has been worrying me.

For the last few weeks, there has been loud music from your flat late at night, often until two or three in the morning. I’m sure you don’t realise how much noise travels between the floors, but I have exams this month and I need to get up early.

I wonder if you could turn the music down after eleven o’clock on weekdays? I would really appreciate it. If it’s easier, I’d be happy to talk about it in person.

Thank you for understanding.

Kind regards,

Nodira Saidova

UNIT 7.1 · MODEL TEXT · HOTEL REVIEW

Review: Silk Road Guest House, Bukhara ★★★★☆

I stayed at Silk Road Guest House for three nights in October, and overall, I was very impressed.

The location is perfect – it’s in the old town, so all the main sights are within walking distance. The rooms are basic but clean, and the beds are very comfortable. What I liked most was the breakfast, which was served on a beautiful terrace with a view of the old city. The staff were incredibly friendly and helped us book a taxi to the airport.

The only downside was the noise from the street in the evening, which was quite annoying. The Wi-Fi was also unreliable.

All things considered, it’s excellent value for money. I would highly recommend it to anyone who wants to experience traditional Uzbek hospitality.

UNIT 9.1 · MODEL TEXT · ARTICLE GIVING ADVICE

Five ways to stay healthy as a student

Do you often feel tired and stressed during exams? You are not alone. Here are five simple ways to look after your health.

First of all, get enough sleep. Experts say that young people need eight to nine hours a night, so try not to stay up late.

Secondly, eat a balanced diet. It’s a good idea to keep healthy snacks, like fruit and nuts, in your bag instead of buying junk food.

Another tip is to stay active. Even a twenty-minute walk every day can improve your fitness and your mood.

You should also take regular breaks when you study, and spend time with friends – your mental health is as important as your physical health.

Finally, don’t forget to drink plenty of water. Follow these tips and you’ll feel the difference in just a few weeks!

UNIT10

Food

Text type: Description of a traditional dish · Opinion essay

4pages
UNIT 10.1 · MODEL TEXT · DESCRIPTION OF A TRADITIONAL DISH

Plov: the heart of Uzbek cooking

If you ever visit Uzbekistan, you must try plov. It is our national dish, and it is served at weddings, birthdays and family celebrations.

Plov is made with rice, lamb, carrots, onions and spices such as cumin. It is cooked in a large, heavy pan called a kazan. First, the meat and onions are fried in hot oil. Then the carrots, cut into thin strips, are added, followed by water and spices. Finally, the rice is put on top and cooked slowly until the water disappears.

The result is a rich, savoury dish with a wonderful flavour. It is usually eaten with fresh salad and green tea.

For many Uzbek families, plov is more than food – it is a way of bringing people together.

  • ServingIt is usually served with … / It is eaten at …
  • SequenceFirst, … Then … After that, … Finally, …

UNIT 11.1 · MODEL TEXT · FORMAL LETTER TO A NEWSPAPER

Letter to the editor: save our park

Dear Editor,

I am writing in response to your article “New car park for city centre” (12 May), which reported that the council plans to replace Bobur Park with a car park.

In my opinion, this would be a serious mistake. Firstly, the park is one of the few green spaces in the city centre, and it is used every day by families, students and elderly people. Furthermore, trees help to reduce air pollution, which is already a major issue in our city.

I understand that parking is a problem. However, I believe a better solution would be to improve public transport, so that fewer people need to drive into the centre.

I hope the council will think again before making a decision that cannot be undone.

Yours faithfully,

Jasur Aliyev

UNIT 11.2 · LANGUAGE FOCUS

Expressing and supporting opinions formally

In a letter to a newspaper, say which article you are responding to, give your opinion clearly, support it with reasons, and suggest a solution. Use formal linking words to connect your ideas.

  • PurposeI am writing in response to your article … / I am writing to express my concern about …
  • OpinionIn my opinion, … / I strongly believe that …

Application: Junior Administrator

Dear Ms Davis,

I am writing to apply for the position of Junior Administrator, which was advertised on your company website.

I graduated from Tashkent State University of Economics last year with a degree in business management. Since then, I have been working as an assistant in a small travel company, where I am responsible for dealing with customer enquiries, writing reports and organising meetings.

I believe I would be suitable for this position because I am well organised and I work well under pressure. I also have excellent computer skills and I speak Uzbek, Russian and English fluently.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss my application at an interview. I have attached my CV.

Yours sincerely,

Shahzod Karimov

COMMON MISTAKES

Ten-second checks before you finish

Don’t writeWriteWhy?
✗ I have seen him yesterday.✓ I saw him yesterday.past simple with finished time
✗ I live here since 2018.✓ I have lived here since 2018.present perfect with since / for
✗ If I will have time, I will call you.✓ If I have time, I will call you.no will after if
✗ Although it was late, but we went out.✓ Although it was late, we went out.although OR but, not both
✗ Despite of the rain, we played.✓ Despite the rain, we played.despite (no of) / in spite of
✗ I look forward to hear from you.✓ I look forward to hearing from you.look forward to + -ing
✗ The people which live here are friendly.✓ The people who live here are friendly.who for people, which for things
✗ Could you tell me where is the station?✓ Could you tell me where the station is?indirect questions: normal word order
✗ I’m interesting in history.✓ I’m interested in history.-ed = feelings, -ing = things
✗ It depends of the weather.✓ It depends on the weather.depend on
✗ In the other hand, …✓ On the other hand, …fixed phrase
✗ The most of people agree.✓ Most people agree.no the before most + noun
✗ I suggest you to take a taxi.✓ I suggest taking a taxi. / I suggest (that) you take …suggest + -ing / that
✗ Everybody have their own opinion.✓ Everybody has their own opinion.everybody + singular verb
✗ Dear Mr Brown, … Yours faithfully,✓ Dear Mr Brown, … Yours sincerely,name known → sincerely
✗ Nowadays people is very busy.✓ Nowadays people are very busy.people is plural

Model answers · Units 1–2

UNIT 1 · WRITING TASK

Letter to an old friend

Dear Maria,

Thanks for your letter – it was great to hear from you! You asked how I spend my free time these days, so here’s my news.

My life has changed a lot since I started working at a bank last autumn. I work long hours, so in the week I don’t have much free time. Still, I try to keep fit – I go swimming twice a week after work.

At the weekend I usually have a lie-in on Saturday and then meet my friends. We often go for a walk in the park or have dinner together. On Sundays I visit my grandparents.

Anyway, why don’t you come to Tashkent in May? We could go hiking in the mountains – the weather is perfect then.

Hope to hear from you soon.

All the best,

Dilnoza

UNIT 1 · ESSAY

Some people say that people today have less free time than in the past. Do you agree or disagree?

It is often said that people today have less free time than in the past. In my opinion, this is true for most people, although technology has also saved us time in some ways.

Firstly, many people now work and study longer hours. For example, students often have extra classes in the evening, and adults may answer work emails at home. As a result, they have very little time to relax.

Secondly, phones and the internet fill every free minute. Instead of resting or meeting friends, people scroll through social media, so their free time does not feel free.

On the other hand, machines and online services save us a lot of time. We can shop, pay bills and order food without leaving home.

In conclusion, although technology helps us in some ways, I believe that most people today have less real free time than previous generations.

UNIT 2 · WRITING TASK

Article: the best and worst of my town

Living in Samarkand: the good and the bad

Imagine a city where every street tells a story. That is Samarkand, my hometown.

The best thing about Samarkand is its history. The Registan, which is in the centre, is breathtaking, especially at night. The city is also safe and friendly, and the food at the bazaar, where I go every Saturday, is delicious and cheap.

However, there are a few problems. There isn’t much nightlife for young people, and the traffic in the city centre is getting worse every year. Some areas also have problems with rubbish.

All in all, I would recommend Samarkand to young people who love culture and history. It is a wonderful place to study, although it can feel a little quiet at the weekend.

UNIT 2 · ESSAY

More and more people are moving from the countryside to big cities. What are the advantages and disadvantages of this?

Nowadays, a growing number of people are leaving the countryside to live in big cities. This trend has both advantages and disadvantages.

The main advantage is that cities offer more opportunities. There are more jobs, universities and hospitals, so people can earn more and get a better education. In addition, cities have better public transport and more entertainment.

However, there are also serious disadvantages. When too many people move to a city, it becomes crowded, polluted and expensive. For example, rents in Tashkent have increased a lot in recent years. Moreover, villages lose their young people, and old traditions may disappear.

In conclusion, moving to a city can improve people’s lives, but governments should also create jobs in the countryside so that villages do not become empty.

© Impulse Learning Center · Topics from Navigate Pre-intermediate B1 Page 56
IMPULSELEARNING CENTER B1 WRITING BOOK

Model answers · Units 3–4

UNIT 3 · WRITING TASK

A story competition

I knew it was going to be a strange day as soon as I woke up. My alarm hadn’t rung, and it was already half past eight!

I jumped out of bed, got dressed quickly and ran to the bus stop. While I was waiting, it started to rain heavily. I had forgotten my umbrella, so I was soon soaking wet and very anxious about being late for my exam.

When I finally arrived at the university, the building was completely empty. I felt confused and frightened. Then a security guard walked towards me and smiled.

“The exam is tomorrow,” he said calmly. I had read the timetable wrongly!

At first I was embarrassed, but then I started laughing. In the end, I went home, had a hot shower and studied for one more day. Luckily, I passed.

UNIT 3 · ESSAY

Some people think it is better to show your emotions, while others think it is better to hide them. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

People have different opinions about whether we should show our emotions or hide them. Both views have some truth in them.

On the one hand, showing emotions can be positive. When we tell others how we feel, they understand us better and can support us. Moreover, psychologists say that hiding feelings for a long time can cause stress and even health problems.

On the other hand, there are situations where it is better to stay calm. At work, for example, shouting at colleagues is unprofessional. In addition, showing strong anger can hurt the people we love.

In my opinion, it is important to express our feelings, but we should do it calmly and at the right time. In conclusion, the best approach is to be honest about emotions while still respecting other people.

UNIT 4 · WRITING TASK

A special moment

The day that changed my life

The day I got my first job will always be special to me. It happened two years ago, when I was nineteen.

At first, I felt anxious and excited at the same time. I had never worked in an office before, and I was afraid of making mistakes. During the first week, I hardly slept!

However, as soon as I got to know my colleagues, everything became easier. They were patient and helpful, and eventually I started to enjoy my work. Since then, I’ve saved enough money to pay for my English course, and I’ve become much more confident.

Looking back, that day taught me that new challenges are frightening only at the beginning. Now I’m not afraid to try new things.

UNIT 4 · ESSAY

Some people think that young people should leave home and live independently as soon as they finish school. Do you agree or disagree?

In many countries, there is a debate about when young people should leave home. I partly agree that it is good to live independently after school, but I do not think it is always possible.

On the one hand, living alone teaches young people important skills. They learn to cook, manage money and take responsibility for their own decisions. As a result, they often become more confident and mature.

On the other hand, rent is very expensive, especially in big cities, so many students cannot afford their own flat. Moreover, in cultures like mine, families traditionally live together for a long time, and young people help their parents.

In conclusion, I believe living independently is a valuable experience, but young people should only leave home when they are ready and can support themselves.

Model answers · Units 5–6

UNIT 5 · WRITING TASK

A problem with a service

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about the service at your City Centre gym, where I paid for a one-month membership on 1 May (membership number 3051).

Unfortunately, there have been several problems. Firstly, half of the running machines have been broken for three weeks. Secondly, the changing rooms are often dirty, and there is rarely any hot water in the showers. Finally, two of the evening classes were cancelled without warning.

As a result, I have only been able to use the gym a few times, and I feel that I have wasted my money.

I would be grateful if you could repair the equipment as soon as possible and give me a partial refund for this month.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,

Aziz Rakhimov

UNIT 5 · ESSAY

In the future, cash will disappear and people will pay for everything by card or phone. What are the advantages and disadvantages of a cashless society?

Many people believe that in the near future cash will disappear completely. A cashless society would have both benefits and drawbacks.

The biggest advantage is convenience. Paying by card or phone is fast, and people do not need to carry coins and notes. In addition, there would be fewer robberies, and it would be easier to keep a record of our spending, which could help people save money.

However, there are also disadvantages. Older people, who are not used to technology, may find it difficult to pay without cash. Moreover, if the internet or the bank system stops working, people might not be able to buy even basic things like food.

In conclusion, a cashless society would make life easier for most people, but it is important to keep cash as an option for those who need it.

UNIT 6 · WRITING TASK

Letter to a flatmate or neighbour

Dear Jamshid,

I hope you don’t mind me writing to you instead of talking, but I wanted to explain something clearly.

As you know, we agreed to share the cleaning when we moved in. However, for the last month the kitchen has been very messy, and the rubbish often stays in the flat for days. I’m sure you are busy with your studies, but I have been doing most of the cleaning myself.

This is quite stressful for me, especially now that I have a part-time job.

I wonder if we could make a simple cleaning timetable? For example, one of us could clean the kitchen on Mondays and the other on Thursdays. I’d be happy to talk about it this evening.

Thanks for understanding.

Best wishes,

Bobur

UNIT 6 · ESSAY

Some people say that social media makes our relationships weaker. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Social media has become a central part of our lives, and some people believe it is damaging our relationships. I agree with this to some extent, but I also think it has important benefits.

On the one hand, many people now spend time on their phones instead of talking face to face. For example, it is common to see friends in a café who are all looking at their screens. Moreover, online friendships are often not very deep.

On the other hand, social media helps us keep in touch with family and friends who live far away. My cousin lives in Korea, but we talk every week. It can also help shy people to make friends.

In conclusion, I believe social media can weaken relationships if we use it too much, but used carefully, it can bring people closer together.

© Impulse Learning Center · Topics from Navigate Pre-intermediate B1 Page 58
IMPULSELEARNING CENTER B1 WRITING BOOK

Model answers · Units 7–8

UNIT 7 · WRITING TASK

Review a place you stayed in

Review: Mountain View Hostel, Chimgan ★★★☆☆

I stayed at Mountain View Hostel for two nights last summer with three friends.

The location is fantastic – it’s surrounded by mountains and the views from the balcony are breathtaking. Our room was small but clean, and the beds were comfortable. The best thing was the friendly owner, who cooked a delicious dinner for us and gave us useful advice about hiking routes.

However, there were a few annoying problems. The shower was often cold, and the Wi-Fi hardly ever worked. It is also quite remote, so you need a car to get there.

All things considered, it’s a relaxing place and good value for money. I would recommend it to young people who love nature and don’t mind basic accommodation.

UNIT 7 · ESSAY

Some people believe that international tourism does more harm than good to local communities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

International tourism has grown enormously in recent years. Although it can cause problems, I disagree that it does more harm than good to local communities.

Firstly, tourism creates jobs and brings money to the area. Hotels, restaurants and shops need workers, and local craftspeople can sell their products. For example, in Bukhara many families earn a living from tourism.

Secondly, tourism helps people from different countries understand each other’s cultures, which is important in today’s world.

It is true that too many tourists can cause pollution and make prices higher for local people. However, these problems can be reduced if governments plan tourism carefully.

In conclusion, I believe that, when it is well managed, tourism brings more benefits than problems to local communities.

UNIT 8 · WRITING TASK

Asking about a course

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to enquire about the photography course for beginners which I saw advertised on your website. I have recently bought my first camera and I would like to learn how to take professional photos.

I would be grateful if you could send me some more information. In particular, I would like to know when the summer course starts and how many lessons there are each week. Could you also tell me whether the classes take place in the evening?

In addition, I was wondering how many students there are in each group and whether the teachers are professional photographers.

Finally, could you let me know how much the course costs and if it is possible to pay online?

Thank you in advance for your help.

Yours faithfully,

Kamila Usmonova

UNIT 8 · ESSAY

Some people think that online learning will soon replace traditional classrooms. Do you agree or disagree?

With the growth of the internet, online learning has become very popular, and some people believe it will soon replace traditional classrooms. I do not agree with this view.

It is true that online learning has many advantages. It is flexible, so students can study at any time, and it is often cheaper. Moreover, learners can take courses from excellent teachers anywhere in the world.

However, I believe classrooms will always be necessary. Children need face-to-face contact to develop social skills, such as working in a team. In addition, practical subjects like chemistry or sport are very difficult to learn through a screen. Many students also find it hard to stay motivated at home.

In conclusion, online learning is a useful addition to education, but I do not think it will replace traditional classrooms completely.

IMPULSELEARNING CENTER B1 WRITING BOOK

Model answers · Units 9–10

UNIT 9 · WRITING TASK

Advice for new students

How to have a healthy first year at college

Starting college is exciting, but it can also be stressful. Do you want to stay healthy and enjoy your first year? Then read on!

First of all, try to eat a balanced diet. It’s a good idea to cook simple meals at home instead of eating fast food every day. You should also go to bed at a regular time – your brain needs sleep to remember what you have learned.

Another tip is to join a sports club. Exercise is a great way to reduce stress, and you’ll make new friends too. If you feel worried about exams, talk to someone instead of keeping it inside.

Follow these tips and you’ll have a healthy, happy and successful first year!

UNIT 9 · ESSAY

Many people today do not get enough physical exercise. What are the causes of this problem, and what can be done to solve it?

Nowadays, many people do not get enough physical exercise, which can lead to serious health problems. This essay will look at the causes of this situation and suggest some solutions.

The main cause is modern lifestyles. Many people sit at desks and computers all day, both at work and at home. In addition, people often drive everywhere, even for very short journeys, instead of walking or cycling.

There are several ways to solve this problem. Firstly, schools and companies could offer short exercise breaks and sports clubs. Secondly, governments should build more parks and safe cycle lanes, so that being active becomes easier. Finally, people can make small changes, such as taking the stairs instead of the lift.

In conclusion, although modern life makes us less active, there are simple solutions that could help people become healthier.

UNIT 10 · WRITING TASK

A dish from my country

Manti

Manti is one of the most popular dishes in Uzbekistan. It is eaten all year round, but especially at family dinners and celebrations.

Manti are large steamed dumplings. The filling is made with chopped lamb or beef, onions, a little fat and spices such as black pepper and cumin.

First, a simple dough is made from flour, water and salt. Then it is rolled out very thinly and cut into squares. A spoonful of filling is put on each square, and the edges are folded together. After that, the manti are cooked in a special steamer for about forty minutes. Finally, they are served with sour cream or tomato sauce.

For me, manti are special because my grandmother taught me how to make them. Every time I eat them, I remember her kitchen.

UNIT 10 · ESSAY

Some people think that governments should put a tax on unhealthy food to make people eat more healthily. Do you agree or disagree?

In many countries, unhealthy diets are causing serious health problems, and some people believe a tax on unhealthy food is the solution. I partly agree with this idea.

On the one hand, a tax could change people’s habits. If junk food becomes more expensive, people will probably buy less of it. Moreover, the government could use the money to pay for hospitals or build sports centres.

On the other hand, a tax would affect poor families most, because they often depend on cheap food. In addition, I believe education is more effective than higher prices. If children learn about healthy eating at school, they will make better choices for the rest of their lives.

In conclusion, a tax on unhealthy food might help, but it should be combined with education about healthy eating.

Model answers · Units 11–12

UNIT 11 · WRITING TASK

Your opinion about a local issue

Dear Editor,

I am writing in response to your article “Library to close” (3 March), which reported that the city plans to replace the public library with a shopping centre.

I strongly believe that this plan is a mistake. Firstly, the library is the only quiet place in our town where students can study for free. Many young people do not have space to study at home. Furthermore, the library organises free English and computer classes for elderly people.

I understand that the building is old and expensive to run. However, I believe a better solution would be to modernise the library and add a small café, so that it could earn some money.

We already have two shopping centres in our town, but only one library. I hope the council will think again.

Yours faithfully,

Malika Tursunova

UNIT 11 · ESSAY

Some people believe that environmental problems are too big for individuals to solve and only governments can help. To what extent do you agree or disagree?

Environmental problems such as global warming and pollution are some of the biggest challenges today. Some people think only governments can solve them, but I believe individuals also have an important role.

It is true that governments have the most power. They can make laws, control factories and invest in clean energy. Large projects, like building metro systems, also need a lot of money that only governments have.

However, individuals can make a real difference too. We can recycle, save energy at home and use less plastic. For example, if millions of people stop using plastic bags, the amount of rubbish will fall dramatically. In addition, when people change their habits, governments often follow.

In conclusion, I believe governments and individuals must work together to protect the environment.

I believe I would be suitable for this job because I am energetic, patient and good at working in a team. I also speak English and Russian fluently, which would help me communicate with teenagers from different countries.

I am available for an interview at any time after 20 May. I have attached my CV.

Yours faithfully,

Nigora Rashidova

UNIT 12 · ESSAY

Some people prefer to work for a large company, while others prefer to be self-employed. Discuss both views and give your opinion.

Some people prefer the security of working for a large company, while others would rather be their own boss. Both choices have advantages.

On the one hand, large companies offer a regular salary, holidays and training. They also usually have clear career paths, so employees can be promoted over time. For many people, especially those with families, this security is very important.

On the other hand, self-employed people are free to make their own decisions and choose their working hours. If their business is successful, they can also earn more money. However, it can be risky and stressful, because there is no guaranteed income.

In my opinion, young people should first work for a large company to gain experience. Later, when they have enough knowledge and savings, they can start their own business.
